column2: Software Development using AI
UG

This course examines modern AI-native software development, focusing on how developers collaborate with coding agents. Designed for third- and fourth-year undergraduate students, the curriculum covers defining intent, structuring development workflows, and coordinating AI tools. Students learn to configure AI-assisted environments, translate high-level functional requirements into executable specifications, and analyze execution traces to diagnose agent-driven workflow failures. Additionally, they evaluate the correctness, reliability, and security risks of agent-generated code, and benchmark end-to-end software pipelines. The course is taught through three hours of lectures, one tutorial hour, and two practical lab hours per week, culminating in a hands-on project. Crucially, this is a practical, workflow-oriented engineering course rather than a general introduction to artificial intelligence, a traditional programming class, or a purely theoretical treatment of large language models.

Course Code: Configure AI-assisted development environments and coding agents for a supplied software task, utilizing tool use and MCP protocols, such that all public integration tests pass and no warnings are generated by the static analyzer.
column2: Translate high-level functional requirements into executable specifications and structured prompt contexts, for a given software project of moderate complexity, covering every use case in the supplied requirements document.
column3: Analyse agent-driven development workflows and loop execution failures, identifying at least three distinct failure causes with supporting log evidence from the execution trace.
column4: Evaluate the correctness, reliability, and security risks of agent-generated code using automated testing and evaluation benchmarks, identifying at least three seeded security or functional defects with a proposed fix for each.
column5: Evaluate an end-to-end AI-native software development process integrating coding agents, automated testing, and deployment pipelines, benchmarking the system performance with at least two scenario walkthroughs chosen by the evaluator.
